title: picture, source, srcset, sizes
learningObjectives: Explain picture, source, srcset, sizes and create scalable, accessible graphics or media markup.

understand.concept: The picture element provides multiple image sources for art direction or format selection. source elements can specify media conditions or MIME types. srcset and sizes on img allow the browser to choose an appropriate resource from candidates based on the display slot and device characteristics.
understand.whyItMatters: Responsive images can reduce bandwidth and deliver a composition suited to the viewport. Always keep an img fallback with meaningful alt text and test that the selected image is appropriate.
understand.analogy: Responsive image markup gives the browser a set of suitable image choices rather than forcing one file into every context.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual vector, bitmap, and accessibility behaviour follows the relevant graphics and browser specifications.

explain.narrative: The browser selects a matching source where available and uses the img source as fallback. Replace illustrative paths with real permitted image assets.

examples.explanation: The browser selects a matching source where available and uses the img source as fallback. Replace illustrative paths with real permitted image assets.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered SVG, canvas, or responsive image example.

practise.guidedTask: Create a picture element with a wide art-directed source and a default img. Add srcset and sizes to a separate responsive image example.
practise.independentTask: Create a small graphic or responsive media example. Include accessible naming or equivalent text and test different display sizes.
hints: Keep important information available as HTML.
Use viewBox for SVG coordinate systems.
Test responsive source selection and image alternatives.

questions.prompt: Which element remains the required fallback content inside picture?
questions.explanation: picture uses an img child as its fallback and accessible image content.

questions.prompt: What is a good accessibility practice for meaningful graphics?
options: Provide an accessible name or equivalent information
questions.answer: Provide an accessible name or equivalent information
questions.explanation: Meaningful visual information must also be available through accessible text or equivalent content.
